sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: blinded_decrypt
tools.description:
Decrypts the message using blinding to prevent side-channel attacks.
    
    :param n: RSA modulus
    :param e: RSA public exponent
    :param d: RSA private exponent
    :param p: First prime factor of n
    :param q: Second prime factor of n
    :param encrypted: the encrypted message
    :type encrypted: int
    
    :returns: the decrypted message
    :rtype: int
    
    Example: blinded_decrypt(1024, 65537, 65537, 31, 33, 123) -> decrypted message

tools.name: get_integer_bit_size
tools.description: Calculate the number of bits needed to represent an integer. num: Integer value. If num is 0, returns 0. Only the absolute value of the number is considered.

tools.name: get_integer_byte_size
tools.description: Calculate the number of bytes required to store an integer. number: An unsigned integer -> The number of bytes required to hold the integer.

tools.name: extended_euclidean_algorithm
tools.description: Returns a tuple (r, i, j) such that r = gcd(a, b) = ia + jb. Example: extended_euclidean_algorithm(30, 18) -> (6, -1, 2)

tools.name: modular_inverse
tools.description:
Returns the inverse of x % n under multiplication, a.k.a x^-1 (mod n)
    
    Args:
        x: The integer to find the modular multiplicative inverse of
        n: The modulus
    
    Returns:
        The modular multiplicative inverse of x modulo n
    
    Example:
        >>> modular_inverse(7, 4)
        3

tools.name: encrypt_integer
tools.description: Encrypts a message using encryption key 'ekey', working modulo n. message: The integer message to encrypt, ekey: The RSA encryption key, n: The modulus for RSA encryption. Example: encrypt_integer(123, 5, 1000) -> 827

tools.name: decrypt_integer
tools.description: Decrypts a cypher text using the decryption key 'dkey', working modulo n. cyphertext: The encrypted integer to decrypt, dkey: The RSA private decryption exponent, n: The RSA modulus, e.g. decrypt_integer(123, 456, 789) -> 678.

tools.name: generate_prime_number
tools.description:
Generate a prime number that fits within a specified number of bits.
    
    Args:
        nbits: The number of bits for the generated prime number
        
    Returns:
        A prime number that can be stored in 'nbits' bits
        
    Example:
        >>> generate_prime_number(128)
        123456789012345678901234567890123456789

tools.name: check_coprime
tools.description:
Returns True if a and b are relatively prime, and False if they are not.
    
    Args:
        a: First integer to check
        b: Second integer to check
    
    Example:
        >>> check_coprime(2, 3)
        True

tools.name: read_random_integer
tools.description: Reads a random integer of approximately nbits bits. nbits: The approximate number of bits for the random integer, e.g. read_random_integer(8) -> 173.

tools.name: read_random_odd_integer
tools.description:
Reads a random odd integer of approximately nbits bits.
    
    Args:
        nbits: The approximate number of bits for the random odd integer
        
    Returns:
        A random odd integer with approximately nbits bits
        
    Example:
        >>> read_random_odd_integer(512) & 1
        1
